title: Destruction of Idols and False Prophets
english: Sprinkling. On many a day already spoken of, with clarity, regarding others it will be so: every place in the house of David in Jerusalem will be opened, a movement occurring toward a divine sprinkling.

But the place being opened in the house of David is the God-breathed Scripture, especially that before the coming of the Savior; the place being opened is this Jerusalem, which is the heavenly and the mother of the righteous, existing as the 'city of the heavenly God of the living.'

In these things, the place to be omitted is not the body that circumscribes and limits, but that which divides into propositions and problems. The intellect will see a movement of these thus-treated places from the letter toward the spirit and from the shadow toward the truth; and, having summed it up, one might say, from the temporal toward the eternal, from the visible and low things toward the high and invisible.

And what follows the movement, or a pouring-over bringing perfect purification? This sprinkling is accomplished by the blood of the Savior, concerning which writes Peter, the most preeminent of the apostles, addressing those to whom he sends the epistle, saying: 'Grace to you and peace be multiplied, for the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ' (1 Peter 1:2).

The divine blood sprinkles the conscience of those worshiping the living God, 'redeeming from the empty manner of received tradition' (1 Peter 1:18) those who are performing [it], as the wise instructor presents in the same epistle, thus: 'Knowing that not with corruptible things, silver or gold, were you redeemed, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot' (1 Peter 1:18-19).

Those pouring over toward the acquisition of a pure heart, repeatedly and continuously entreating toward the ability to desire purity, as one says: 'Wash me, and I shall become whiter than snow' (Psalm 51:7). Toward this purity, 'being a pure and undefiled worship' (James 1:27), the holy word exhorts: 'Wash, that you may become clean' (Ezekiel 36:25), it advises.

If the love of this spoken pouring-over enters even us, let us hasten to dwell as citizens in the intelligible Jerusalem being ruled by David, so that every interpreted place may be opened to us, having been moved from the shadowy toward the original and true wise contemplations.
On that day, the Lord says, 'I will destroy the names of the idols from the earth and they shall no more be a memory; and the false prophets and the unclean spirit I will remove from the earth.'

When the previously foretold movement becomes a sprinkling and the truth, the various forms of the heterodox, called idols tropically, shall be destroyed from the earth, no longer deceiving men, the tropical idolatry being exposed by the revealed truth and all false prophecy being annulled and the unclean spirit working it, being present in man before the faith into Christ.

It is also possible to say concerning the sensible idols and the demons concerning them that they shall be destroyed from the earth. But that the statues are indicated by this designation, it is possible to learn from the hymn-singer saying: 'The idols of the Gentiles, silver and gold, they have feet and they do not walk' (Psalm 115:4), and the following. That the demons defiling their shrines are called by the same name, the prophet Isaiah teaches beginning from there: 'Demolish, the carved images in Jerusalem and in Samaria; for in the same way as I did in Samaria and with its carved images, so will I do to Jerusalem and to its idols' (Isaiah 2:18).

In demolishing idols, both carved and cast, it is not the works of craftsmen that are being demolished, nor things that are natural to be demolished; for the energy is breathing life into them. For the demolition is a meaningless sound emitted by an animal by a passion of the soul. This meaning has been demonstrated in many ways in the memoirs concerning Isaiah, with the testimony of Solomon the Wise, having it thus: 'For equally hated by God are the impious man and his impiety; for what has been done with the doer shall be punished' (Wisdom 1:13).

These things were said to the wise man concerning a carpenter man and carved wood by him according to the form of an animal, and just as it is not able to demolish that which does not have a soul, as it was called a mere shadow, so it is not able to be punished effectively. Therefore, let these things be taken up concerning the demons wandering about with the soulless statues. While the idols are being destroyed from the earth, the false diviners and those who once promised false predictions are removed from it, false prophets in judgment by the divine.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Shame of the False Prophet
english: Being called for instruction, he is being convinced of this same thing along with them and of the unclean spirit. For how can the spirit of the diviners and bird-diviners not have the impurity which comes from impiety?

This same word could also be applied to the protectors of heresies, who have happened to be full of demons and deceiving spirits. For regarding them the Lawgiver Paul writes thus: 'Some will depart from the healthy faith, paying attention to deceiving spirits and demonic teachings, in the hypocrisy of false prophets, having been cauterized in their own conscience' (1 Timothy 4:2).

It is not to be disturbed if the unclean spirit is spoken of in the singular in the prophet, but the deceiving spirits are spoken of in the plural in the Apostolic Scripture. For those things which are taken individually according to each are generally called one spirit. And it is also good to say that the naming of the names of idols is being destroyed, as if their mention were no longer to be, because of their vanity and foolishness, even though they exist only as a designation and not as a power.

Zach. XIII, 3: 'And it shall come to pass, if a man prophesies any more, his father and his mother who begot him will say to him, "You shall not live, because you have spoken falsely in the name of the Lord"'; and his father and his mother who begot him will run against him in his prophesying (Zechariah 13:3).

Once the false prophets and the unclean spirit have been removed from the earth, if a man should still dare to prophesy out of frenzy and madness, he would be so much a laughingstock and subject to rebuke, that even his parents would not believe him, but would vote for his death, announcing: 'He shall not live anymore because he has spoken falsely upon the name of the Lord,' he being found not a prophet but a false prophet.
By these things, the false prophet is rebuked by his father and his mother, who run against him and join in his downfall, rebuking his sophistries and his deceptive words.

Because the phrase 'those who begot him in his prophesying' is ambiguous, it should be expanded into both meanings. One way it might be understood: those who begot him as a man have a disposition toward him as humans guarding parents, because he speaks falsely in the name of the Lord, and they join in his downfall by voting against him. The other way it might be attributed thus: his father and his mother...

They join in mockery against him, those who brought him forth into prophesying, having fathered him as a false prophet through upbringing and procreation, having generated him through imitation and teaching, and who are clearly possessed of a false-prophetic disposition.

It is not in vain that such an 'man' has been reproved; rather, because he walks falsely 'in strife and jealousy' according to the flesh, he holds the name of man, similar to those to whom it was said, 'You indeed die as men' (1 Cor 3:4), and concerning those unworthy of the Divine Spirit, the Lord says, 'My Spirit shall not remain in these men because they are flesh' (Rom 8:9).

Zechariah 13:4–6: And on that day the prophets shall be ashamed, each from his vision in his prophesying, and they shall put on haircloth instead of those [garments] by which they lied. And he shall say, 'I am not a prophet, because a man has fathered me from my youth.' And I will say to him, 'Why are these wounds between your hands?' And he shall say, 'Those which were struck in my beloved house.'

Those who promise foreknowledge experience shame because their pre-proclamation is falling away. Since, therefore, the indictment of the false prophet comes not from others alone but also from those who fathered him, for this reason he is ashamed, his prophecy having been exposed, so that he is left to revile himself and to be clothed in haircloth. For a man confesses that he has existed from youth, the youth of which now denotes not age but a young and impetuous character.

For the wicked one, not possessing prudent wisdom nor honorable old age, nor a life without blemish, passes through life with ignorance, according to the proverbial saying: 'Folly is widespread in the heart of a youth, and a rod and instruction are far from him' (Prov 13:24). He, finding this state to be the worst, offers a plea to God: 'Do not remember the sinfulness of my youth and my ignorance' (Ps 25:7).

He who is exposed as speaking falsely in prophesying, being ashamed of his vain vision—which is more like divination than true prophecy—confesses that he is not a prophet nor was he advanced from among the prophets to this.

title: The Shepherd and the Sheep
english: Wounds between your two hands? Regarding that which he says: 'She was struck in the house of my beloved,' even those who begot me are not enduring [it] as a prophet, as if bringing wounds against me.

It is possible to call the house of the beloved the house of the false prophet, knowing the multitude loved by him who divines, in order to subject him to afflictions. And these things are to be applied to those who hold different opinions in Christianity.

The false repentance of one wearing sackcloth is brought in [the context of] Isaiah against those fasting and praying, becoming a rebuke against the hypocrites: 'For if you bow your neck like a yoke and bend your neck and put on sackcloth and ashes, you will not even call it a pleasing fast' (Isa 58:5). I do not say this as if no one benefits from the painful discipline and harsh diet, which then becomes beneficial when it is accomplished along with repentance.

The Ninevites, indeed, having repented with much wickedness according to the preaching of the prophet Jonah (Jonah 3), have escaped after the threat of a great destruction of their city. The hymn-writer also agrees, where he says: 'In that they were bothering me,' making the enemies both visible and invisible apparent, 'I put on sackcloth and they were humbling my soul in fasting' (Ps 69:13), and in another Psalm: 'I made my clothing sackcloth, and I became a parable to them' (Ps 69:34).

From this state thus occurring, of gloominess for the sake of acquiring good things, he who attains them, having changed into joy, says: 'You have turned my mourning into joy, you have torn my sackcloth and girded me with gladness' (Ps 30:11).

Zechariah XII, 7: 'A sword, has arisen against my shepherd and against the man, the citizen of him, says the Lord of hosts: Strike the shepherd and let the sheep be scattered, and I will strike my hand upon the shepherds.'

From this prophecy, the evangelist Matthew took up what was said in the Gospel according to him, when, Jesus having been seized, the disciples having been scandalized and having fled, he said: 'So that what was said through the prophet might be fulfilled: I will strike the shepherd and the sheep will be scattered' (Matt 26:31), saying strike and wound the death of the shepherd of the true flock, who is above reason, 'having laid down his soul.'

"himself for the sheep," "given as a ransom for many." Regarding the assault that occurred in this way, where the hands of the excellent lawgiver were struck and his feet were dug up, it is his own to hear the Father saying: "Whom you struck, they themselves persecuted, and upon the pain of my wounds they themselves added" (Psalm 21:6). For the murderers, having struck the one whom God delivered over to them, added to the pain of his wounds, increasing the assault while pursuing him.

The holy thing attempted by the wicked—the one who, setting himself forward for the sheep, stood as a protector, having the Hebrew people as his citizen—the drawn sword was raised against his own shepherd and his citizen. Thus, the drawn sword killed indeed the citizen, but did not harm the shepherd of the flock, having accepted death for the sake of the sparing of the flock.

For how could he, the one affirming to God, "Save my soul from the sword" (Psalm 34:13), not remain free from all harm? This voice is carried in the twenty-first Psalm, spoken from the person of the whole Savior being brought forth. Having had the soul saved from the sword after sending up the prayer, his citizen fell by the sword of execution, according to that which was said in Amos the prophet: "Let all sinners of the people perish by the sword" (Amos 9:4). The same punishment is alluded to by the prophet in Wisdom by God: "You, Ethiopians, are wounded by my sword" (Wisdom 9:13).

Those being struck by the sword of God are called Ethiopians, those who shared in the wickedness and sin of the devil, being named so from his blackness. For in the Shepherd and in the Epistle of Barnabas, Satan is approached as black, having fallen from brightness and virtue and the intellectual whiteness which only the one being whitened by God can have.

Having the shepherd struck in the said manner and because of this the sheep being scattered, he stretches out his hand toward the shepherds, the high priest and the elders and the Jewish law-teachers who agreed against the good shepherd having been set forth for the sheep, so that they might have his soul's salvation. And the scattering of the sheep has increased, and the [hand] of God being stretched out upon them and the flock under them...
